Action Plan:
1. Treat presumptive acute gastroenteritis with supportive measures: oral rehydration (oral rehydration solution), increased clear fluid intake, and soft diet (soup, mashed foods) as tolerated.
2. Recommend over-the-counter oral rehydration product (Dioralyte) — patient to purchase from pharmacy (no prescription needed).
3. Symptomatic analgesia/antipyretic: continue Paracetamol as needed (Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented).
4. Advice: avoid alcohol while symptomatic.
5. Safety-net and follow-up: patient to contact clinician if symptoms do not settle within 48 hours or earlier if signs of dehydration develop; if dehydration suspected, further assessment/investigations will be arranged.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: three days of profuse watery diarrhea.
- Onset/duration/progression: symptoms began ~3 days ago and have not improved.
- Stool description/frequency: very watery stools, occurring approximately hourly when awake; no recollection of blood in stool.
- Abdominal pain: crampy lower/central abdominal pain that is intermittent; patient estimates pain severity around 6/10 when it occurs.
- Nausea/vomiting: nausea present; one episode of vomiting after drinking milk.
- Fever: subjective feeling of being very warm; no measured temperature recorded.
- Urine: passing urine less frequently than usual but still passing.
- Possible exposure: brother has had similar illness for ~5 days.
- Oral intake: fluids perceived to pass straight through; had lunch today but stool remained loose.
- Past medical history: reports otherwise fit and well; no regular medications.
- Current medications: occasional Paracetamol taken recently (Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: none known by patient.
- Family history: father with colon cancer (reported stage 3).
- Social history: lives with mother and sister; works in a government office in Central London; smokes socially (occasionally); alcohol use: occasional drinking with heavier episodes once or twice a month.
- Impact: difficulty managing at work due to symptoms; prefers to continue working if possible.

Objective:
- No physical examination findings recorded in transcript.
- No vital signs documented.
- No investigations performed or results available in transcript.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhoea / gastroenteritis:
   - Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis (clinical impression stated by clinician).
   - Differential diagnosis: viral gastroenteritis, foodborne bacterial gastroenteritis, lactose intolerance exacerbation (vomiting after milk) — (differential listed as applicable).
   - Investigations planned: none immediate; reassess if not improving in 48 hours or sooner if concern for dehydration — at that point consider clinical examination, vital signs, blood tests and/or stool studies as indicated.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Oral rehydration: advise oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) from pharmacy (Dioralyte — dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Encourage frequent clear fluids and electrolyte replacement.
     - Diet: clear fluids initially, progress to soft foods (soup, mashed foods) as tolerated.
     - Symptomatic: Paracetamol for fever/pain (Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Avoid alcohol while symptomatic.
   - Referrals: none at this time.

2. Risk of dehydration:
   - Assessment: Risk of dehydration due to frequent watery stools and reduced urine frequency.
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A (risk condition).
   - Investigations planned: not immediate; review and arrange investigations if clinical signs of dehydration or lack of improvement.
   - Treatment planned: oral rehydration as above; patient advised to monitor fluid intake and urine output.
   - Referrals: urgent assessment if dehydration suspected.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, orthostatic measurements), physical abdominal examination findings, stool inspection/culture results, exact doses/routes/frequencies for Paracetamol and Dioralyte, weight/height, pregnancy status if applicable, and formal allergy list.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: patient fluctuated when describing pain severity (initially described as manageable, later estimated ~6/10) — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality comment: audio/visual connection issues noted by patient; parts of the conversation had brief unclear segments but overall history and plans were understandable.
